Text Appearing Before Image:
164 CALIFORNIA FISH AND GAME
Text Appearing After Image:
Pig. 69. A six and one-quarter pound mullet. Schools of small mrillpt oaii frequently be seen in the river where their habit of schooling and leaping makes them easily recognizable. They are often to be seen at Laguna Dam ascending the weir in a thin sheet of water. The mnddiest waters of the Alamo and New rivers seem to be to their liking as are their small partially cut-off lakes where the water is brackish and the temperature high. Mullet are numerous in the quiet canals and drain ditches of the Yuma Project, in the Imperial Valley, and thrive in the highly saline waters of the Salton Sea. In all of these waters they are one of the most abundant fishes. Size. Several hundred mullet were taken in gill-nets in the river (between the International Boundary and Imperial Dam) and near the -heads of canals diverting from it in January, February and May, 1942. The range in size of these fish was 7.8 to 15.6 inches.^^ Most of these mullet appeared to belong to a size group of about 12 inches in length.
